verdicts.title: Fixed-clipping aux and stats types are split asymmetrically across the two stack type façades, so each stack cannot name its own return types
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced every link in the current tree with the repo .venv. packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/dpsgd/clipping/types.py:21-31 has __all__ = [AdaptiveClipState, AdaptiveClippedGradAux, AutoClipState, AutoClippedFunAux, AutoClippedGradAux, ClippingStats, ClippedGradFn, ClippedGradResult, FixedClipState] and does not import ClippedGradAux / ClippedFunAux / ClipPytreeAux at all; packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/dpftrl/clipping/types.py:16-26 has the mirror set (ClipPytreeAux, ClippedFunAux, ClippedGradAux present, ClippingStats absent). `from opaque.dpsgd.clipping.types import ClippedGradAux` and `from opaque.dpftrl.clipping.types import ClippingStats` both raise ImportError (reproduced verbatim). opaque.dpsgd.clipping.clipped_grad is opaque.dpftrl.clipping.clipped_grad -> True, and a real call on both stacks returns the same objects: return_aux=True -> opaque.api.engine.clipping._clipped_grad.ClippedGradAux, return_stats=True -> opaque.api.engine.clipping._clipped_fun.ClippingStats, on BOTH façades. The asymmetry is therefore not a partition of behavior — both types are produced on both stacks. It is also broader than the finding states: opaque.dpsgd.clipping.fun exports clipped_fun / clip_pytree, whose aux types (ClippedFunAux, ClipPytreeAux) are likewise unnameable from opaque.dpsgd.clipping.types. Both modules' ancestors (opaque.api.engine.clipping.types) export the full set, so this is drift in the two hand-written façade lists, not a design boundary. docs/reference/clipping.md:32-33 documents ClippedGradAux and ClippedFunAux as public aux types and :89 renders opaque.dpsgd.clipping.types, which cannot show them. No privacy, numerical or runtime impact: annotation/import ergonomics only, with a working (if cross-stack or opaque.api.*) fallback. No open tracked issue covers it (#968/#880 are LoRA kernel work; nothing in the open lists touches the clipping type façades). Severity low is correct.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A DP-SGD user annotating a training step writes `from opaque.dpsgd.clipping.types import ClippedGradAux` and gets ImportError, even though `opaque.dpsgd.clipping.clipped_grad(..., return_aux=True)` returns exactly that class; symmetrically `from opaque.dpftrl.clipping.types import ClippingStats` raises ImportError while `opaque.dpftrl.clipping.clipped_grad(..., return_stats=True)` returns ClippingStats. Both reproduced in the current tree. Same for ClippedFunAux / ClipPytreeAux on the DP-SGD side despite opaque.dpsgd.clipping.fun exporting clipped_fun / clip_pytree. Workaround is to import from the other stack's façade or from the private opaque.api.engine tree. No effect on privacy accounting, clipping behavior or numerics.

verdicts.title: docs/reference/accounting.md names `opaque.accounting.calibration` a submodule, but only the internal module object is re-exported and `import opaque.accounting.calibration` fails
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced. packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/accounting/ contains only __init__.py, types.py and py.typed; the __init__ does `from opaque.api.accounting.core import (..., amplification, calibration, composition, discretization, mechanisms, ...)` and lists all five in __all__. At runtime each is the internal module object (`opaque.accounting.calibration.__name__ == 'opaque.api.accounting.core.calibration'`, likewise for the other four), so `from opaque.accounting import calibration` works but `import opaque.accounting.calibration` raises ModuleNotFoundError — verified for all five names. docs/reference/accounting.md:677 literally says "Submodule: `opaque.accounting.calibration`" (the only such label in docs/). The contrast holds: `import opaque.dpsgd.accounting.amplification`, `opaque.dpsgd.accounting.mechanisms`, `opaque.dpftrl.accounting.amplification`, `opaque.auditing.one_run`, `opaque.patches.kernels` and `opaque.accounting.types` all succeed. Two mitigations keep this low: the code block immediately under the offending line shows the form that actually works (`from opaque.accounting import calibration as cal`), and nothing about accounting math or epsilon is affected. One aggravating detail the finding only implies: the same non-importable paths are used in ~15 Sphinx cross-references inside shipped docstrings (e.g. packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_budgets.py:14 `:func:`~opaque.accounting.calibration.calibrate``, .../core/types.py:11-13 `:mod:`opaque.accounting.{mechanisms,amplification,composition}.types``), so the broken path is user-visible from help()/docs, and tracebacks/repr name opaque.api.accounting.core.* rather than the public path (ARC-003 spirit). Docs/API-shape accuracy issue; not tracked in the open issue lists.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user following docs/reference/accounting.md:677 ("Submodule: `opaque.accounting.calibration`") writes `import opaque.accounting.calibration as cal` and gets ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'opaque.accounting.calibration'. Same for amplification, composition, discretization and mechanisms — all five are attribute re-exports of opaque.api.accounting.core.* rather than real submodules of the public façade (verified), while the sibling façades opaque.dpsgd.accounting.* and opaque.auditing.* do ship real submodules. The attribute form `from opaque.accounting import calibration` works, so the impact is confusion plus ~15 unresolvable :mod:/:func: cross-references in shipped docstrings, and public-path leakage of opaque.api.* in repr/tracebacks. No effect on accounting results.

verdicts.title: min_sep=0 crashes past its own guard: ZeroDivisionError from the Toeplitz strategies, raw ValueError/OverflowError from the Rust-backed ones
verdicts.reasoning: The error-quality core is reproduced exactly. Guards confirmed at packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_toeplitz.py:496 and :537 (`if min_sep <= 0: raise ConfigurationError('min_sep must be positive')`); BandMfStrategy.sensitivity calls minsep_true_max_participations first at _band_mf.py:170-172, which does `max_part_ub = _ceil_div(n, min_sep)` (_sensitivity.py:64) with `_ceil_div` = `-(x // -y)` (:45) and no guard. Measured on n_steps=16 with the repo .venv: band_mf(bands=4) and blt() -> ZeroDivisionError('integer division or modulo by zero') for min_sep=0 and ConfigurationError('min_sep must be positive') for min_sep=-3; bisr(bandwidth=4) and lambda_cgd(lambda_=0.5) (which additionally require max_participations) -> raw ValueError('Invalid parameter: min_sep must be >= 1') for min_sep=0 and raw OverflowError("can't convert negative int to unsigned") for min_sep=-3. `strategy.sensitivity(n_steps=..., min_sep=...)` is documented public API (docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/band-mf.md:74, docs/user-guide/noise.md:494-496), so these are reachable from a documented call site. Two corrections that cut the severity: (1) the privacy-relevant entry point DOES validate — `opaque.dpftrl.accounting.mf_gaussian(1.0, band_mf_strategy(bands=4), n_steps=16, min_sep=0 or -3)` raises ConfigurationError('min_sep must be >= 1, got 0'/'-3'); (2) the finding's claim that mf_gaussian_noise 'defers the failure to whenever the strategy's sensitivity is first needed' is wrong — min_sep is never used for noise generation there: with min_sep in {0, -5, 1, 8} the constructed noise_fn runs and produces bit-identical noise and identical published noise_stddev (1.2580589969236924), because MF noise is min_sep-independent and sensitivity only enters accounting. So the value is silently ignored rather than latently fatal, and no wrong sigma or wrong epsilon can result: everything fails closed or is a no-op. What remains is an error-taxonomy defect (ZeroDivisionError / raw ValueError / raw OverflowError instead of ConfigurationError, and inconsistent across four strategies) on a public method. Not a duplicate of open #359 (BandMF participation sensitivity definition) or #319.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Calling the documented public method `strategy.sensitivity(n_steps=16, min_sep=0)` raises ZeroDivisionError('integer division or modulo by zero') for band_mf_strategy(bands=4) and blt_strategy(), and a raw ValueError('Invalid parameter: min_sep must be >= 1') from the Rust extension for bisr_strategy(bandwidth=4) and lambda_cgd_strategy(lambda_=0.5); min_sep=-3 gives ConfigurationError for the first pair and a raw OverflowError("can't convert negative int to unsigned") for the second. None of these is in the opaque.exceptions taxonomy and the ZeroDivisionError names nothing useful, even though _toeplitz.py:496/:537 hold the correct ConfigurationError guard downstream of the unguarded _ceil_div. The privacy-carrying entry point is unaffected: opaque.dpftrl.accounting.mf_gaussian rejects min_sep<=0 with ConfigurationError, and mf_gaussian_noise ignores min_sep entirely (noise and published stddev are bit-identical for min_sep 0, 1 and 8), so no run can proceed with a wrong sensitivity or a wrong epsilon. Error-message/validation-ordering quality only.

verdicts.title: PEFT/LoRA resume silently restores no adapter weights: the model continues from fresh random init while the accountant, noise counter, sampler cursor and optimizer state are all restored
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end on the real DPTrainer in the repo .venv (peft 0.20.0, transformers 5.15.1). Code: packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:5479-5481 `if not mutated: strict = not self._is_peft; self._model.load_state_dict(new_state, strict=strict)` with the _IncompatibleKeys result discarded and nothing logged; the identical three lines are at :4910-4912 in _load_best_model; _read_weights_file probes 'adapter_model.safetensors' at :4974. self._model is the PeftModel (_is_peft set at :467 from isinstance(PeftModel/PeftMixedModel)), and _save_model_artifacts (:5244-5245) calls self._model.save_pretrained(...), so the checkpoint carries adapter keys with the adapter name stripped. Isolated check: PEFT save_pretrained writes 'base_model.model.lin.lora_{A,B}.weight' while the live module's state_dict has 'base_model.model.lin.lora_{A,B}.default.weight'; load_state_dict(disk, strict=False) returns 2 unexpected / 4 missing keys, changes no parameter, and raises nothing. Full trainer run (tiny GPT-2 + LoRA r=4 on c_attn, batch 4, max_steps 4, save_steps 2, clipping_norm 1.0, noise_multiplier 1.0, use_cpu): checkpoint-2 contains adapter_model.safetensors with the stripped keys plus dp_state.pt, dp_optimizer.pt, accountant.json, rng_state.pth, trainer_state.json; instrumenting _load_model_weights during `train(resume_from_checkpoint=checkpoint-2)` printed `_is_peft: True`, `weights changed by load?: False`, `post-load == checkpoint?: False`, `post-load == fresh-init?: True`, and training then continued to global_step 4 reporting privacy_epsilon 0.8132. Verified there is no second restore path: _apply_runtime_state (:5548-5573) restores clip/noise/optimizer/accountant and only rewrites ctx.trainable_params for ScheduleFreeState, so trainable_params come from the unmutated module. grep confirms set_peft_model_state_dict / get_peft_model_state_dict / load_adapter appear nowhere under packages/ (including opaque-alignment), while HF's own Trainer uses model.load_adapter at .venv/.../transformers/trainer.py:3440 (resume) and :3502 (best model) — the parity DPTrainer claims. I additionally reproduced the load_best_model_at_end=True variant: with eval_steps=2/save_steps=2 and best checkpoint recorded as checkpoint-2, the final in-memory adapter equals checkpoint-4 (last) and NOT checkpoint-2 (best) — the flag silently does nothing for PEFT models, exactly the outcome its own docstring at :4877-4880 says it exists to prevent. Existing resume tests assert only global_step and privacy_epsilon (packages/opaque-transformers/tests/validation/test_dp_guarantees.py:347-349, :567-572), and docs/user-guide/huggingface/dptrainer.md:80-83 documents resume with no caveat. Keeping critical: the failure is silent and total (all learned adapter weights discarded) at the library's primary documented fine-tuning shape, and in a DP setting the wasted budget is not recoverable by re-running — the dataset's privacy budget has been spent on a garbage model. It does require the two explicit opt-ins (a PEFT-wrapped model plus resume_from_checkpoint or load_best_model_at_end), which is the only argument for high rather than critical. affects_epsilon stays false: the reported epsilon is correct for the mechanism actually executed.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: With a PEFT/LoRA-wrapped model (the documented DPTrainer fine-tuning shape), `trainer.train(resume_from_checkpoint='.../checkpoint-N')` restores dp_state.pt, dp_optimizer.pt, accountant.json and the RNG/sampler cursor faithfully, but _dp_trainer.py:5479-5481 calls self._model.load_state_dict(adapter_state, strict=False) on the PeftModel; because PEFT's save_pretrained strips the adapter name ('...lora_A.weight') while the live module's keys carry it ('...lora_A.default.weight'), every saved key is unexpected and every model key missing, the returned _IncompatibleKeys is discarded, and no parameter changes. Reproduced on the real trainer (tiny GPT-2 + LoRA r=4 on c_attn, 4 steps, save_steps=2, resume from checkpoint-2): post-load weights equal the fresh random init and differ from the checkpoint, yet the run completes to global_step 4 and reports privacy_epsilon 0.8132 with no warning. The user gets a plausible-looking completed DP run whose model has thrown away all prior learning while the privacy budget for those steps is permanently spent. The same three lines at :4910-4912 mean load_best_model_at_end=True is also a no-op for PEFT: reproduced with best=checkpoint-2, the final in-memory adapter equals checkpoint-4 (the last checkpoint), not the best one. Non-PEFT full-model checkpoints are unaffected (strict=True).
